newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds close mostly stable.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds close mostly stable.

text.p: Argentine bonds closed generally firm Thursday in quiet trading, dealers said.
"The market eased a bit earlier today and then closed steady after players took profits following yesterday's strong gains," one dealer said.
Local markets were closed Wednesday for Independence Day but Argentine Bradies rose in New York on the back of the U.S. long bond yield's slide to seven-year lows of 6.56 percent, dealers said.
The FRB Brady bond due 2005 closed flat Thursday at 94-7/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 erased early losses and closed up $0.5 at 121.7.

"Volume was decent but shrank as the market fell today, so the session was pretty slow," another trader said. "I think prices will consolidate at these levels now. And if we get any more news on the possible debt buyback scheme mentioned this week by (Economy Minister Roque) Fernandez, then investors may raise their stakes again."
